editorial:
Imagine you are wandering the open road as a man with a giant, angry secret. You get to follow David Banner as he rolls into a small town and finds himself protecting a young heiress from her own greedy family. It feels like a classic mystery mixed with a superhero story. You get this great vibe of a lonely man just trying to do the right thing while hiding a monster inside him. The stakes feel real because Banner is not just fighting bad guys, but he is fighting his own temper and the fear of being caught by a nosy reporter.

You will love how the tension builds up as Jack McGee gets closer to the truth. The acting is solid, and the plot keeps you guessing about who to trust. While some of the special effects look a bit old now, the heart of the story is still there. If you enjoy old-school TV movies with a bit of drama, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, Banner manages to stop the evil stepmother and the doctor from hurting the girl. He uses his strength to save the day but does it in a way that keeps his identity mostly hidden. Jack McGee almost catches him in the act, but Banner slips away just in time. He leaves town once again, still searching for a cure and staying on the run to keep the world safe from the Hulk.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic TV shows and superhero origins.
